To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a tentative 130-GeV {gamma}-ray line signal from the Galactic Center can be explained in terms of dark matter annihila- tion, with a cross section of 1.3×10−27 cm3/s, if the dark matter density profile is cuspy, and that the inner slope of the dark matter density distribution is consistent with the cuspy profile predicted by N-body simulations.
a tentative 130GeV gamma ray line in the Galactic center can be interpreted as a signature of dark matter annihiliation.
the 130 GeV gamma-ray line signal, if real, can be interpreted as dark matter annihilation, and that the inner slope of the dark matter density profile is constrained by the 130 Gev line signal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dark matter distribution in the inner Galaxy and the dark matter interpretation of the 130 GeV gamma-ray line.
the distribution of the dark matter in the very inner Galaxy.
constraining the distribution of dark matter in the inner Galaxy by using an indirect detection signal.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 130 GeV gamma-ray line signal would favor a cuspy dark halo density profile in the inner Galaxy.
the inner dark matter density profile of our Galaxy is not steep, but the data are not yet strong enough to exclude a cusp.
the 130 GeV gamma-ray line signal, if real, would be a very strong hint of dark matter annhilation, and would favor a cuspy dark halo density profile in the inner Galaxy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the 130 GeV gamma-ray line data, if interpreted as a dark matter signal, can only constrain the inner density distribution of the dark matter, but cannot provide a strong test on the nature of the dark matter.
the tentative 130 Gev line signal is not only a smoking gun of dark matter, but also a unique probe of the dark matter distribution in the inner Galaxy.
the tentative gamma-ray line signal, if real, favors a cuspy dark-matter distribution in the inner Galaxy and hence is not consistent with the results from the N-body simulations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a tentative gamma-ray line signal can be used to probe the inner dark matter density profile, which is complementary to the direct constraints from dwarf galaxies.
, in the future, a gamma-ray line signal could be used to constrain dark matter distribution in the inner Galaxy.
, if the signal persists and is confirmed, it will provide the first direct probe of dark matter distribution in the inner region of our Milky Way.
